title: Add KMS correlation IDs and claims-proofing shim for RBAC v2
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve forensic traceability and stronger tenant-bound KMS usage guarantees without changing existing KMS providers. Production incidents showed difficulty correlating KMS operations to a specific tenant claim in multi-tenant hosts (see SUP-9876). This PR introduces an explicit KMS correlation ID propagated through the API stack and a lightweight claims-proofing shim tied to RBAC v2 that verifies a short-lived cryptographic binding between a tenant claim and the KMS request.

Design summary: 1) Add X-Redwood-KMS-Correlation header generation at the ingress proxy for every request that results in a KMS operation. 2) Propagate the correlation ID through the runtime and attach it as audit metadata for all KMS calls. 3) Implement a "claims-proofing shim" in the RBAC v2 evaluation path that verifies a signed ephemeral claim (JWT with KMS usage nonce) provided by the requestor when requesting tenant-scoped keys. 4) Add an audit sampler that marks a configurable percentage of KMS events as "full-provenance" and retains the full correlation chain for longer retention windows. 5) Non-breaking integration with existing KMS adapter interfaces; no provider-specific code required.

What changed (high level): - src/auth/kms_correlation.go: header generation, context propagation helpers, correlation ID lifecycle. - src/security/rbac/shim_claims_proof.go: RBAC shim implementation and policy hooks. - src/observability/audit/sampler.go: sampling decision logic and extended event envelope schema. - pkg/kms/adapter.go: small interface additions (optional metadata map) and adapter adapter tests. - docs/operations/kms-correlation.md: operational runbook and rollout steps. - test/e2e/kms_correlation_test.go: end-to-end test that asserts correlation propagation through a simulated KMS provider.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for correlation helpers and RBAC shim. - [x] E2E test exercising correlation header through runtime to mock KMS. - [x] Docs and runbook for operators to configure sampling and retention. - [x] Backwards compatible: adapters receiving metadata map ignore extra fields if unsupported. - [x] Security review from SEC (SEC-37).

Rollout plan: Gradual opt-in via feature flag `kms_correlation.enabled`. Start with 0.1% sampling in prod and increase to 100% after 2 weeks of monitoring for overhead and false rejections. Key metrics to watch: KMS request latency P99, audit ingestion rate, RBAC rejection rate for claims-proofing.

Impact and caveats: - Adds ~1ms median overhead on KMS paths in Canary due to small context propagation and extra audit writes; measured on perf-canary cluster. - If clients do not provide claims proofs for tenant-scoped CMKs, RBAC shim currently falls back to existing claim checks; we do not fail-open to avoid accidental escalations. - Operators can disable strict claims-proofing via rbac.v2.policy config during rollout.

merge_info: Merged by Diego Morales via squash merge on 2025-11-20. Commit message: 'Add KMS correlation ID propagation and RBAC v2 claims-proofing shim (ENG-1142, SEC-37)'.
release_notes: Introduce tenant-bound KMS correlation IDs and an optional RBAC v2 claims-proofing shim to improve auditability and traceability of KMS operations. Feature gated behind kms_correlation.enabled; rollout instructions in docs/operations/kms-correlation.md.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps adapter changes backward compatible by making the metadata map optional. Follow-up work planned: metrics dashboard (ENG-1160) and support for HSM-backed providers to include provider-signed provenance tokens (SEC-92).
